# onpager_delivery_target (Resource)

Manage one delivery target in an existing OnPager delivery channel. Catalog bindings use the target UUID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "pachca_bot_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "UUID of an enabled Pachca bot in OnPager."
}

variable "pachca_account_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "The bot's addressing_scope_id in Pachca."
}

variable "team_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "UUID of the team receiving the alerts."
}

resource "onpager_delivery_target" "ops_alerts" {
  channel_id = var.pachca_bot_id
  snapshot_json = jsonencode({
    BotID       = var.pachca_bot_id
    Scope       = { Kind = "bot_account", ID = var.pachca_account_id }
    Kind        = "conversation"
    ChannelName = "ops-alerts"
  })
}

resource "onpager_team_alert_channel" "ops_alerts" {
  team_id             = var.team_id
  delivery_channel_id = onpager_delivery_target.ops_alerts.channel_id
  target_id           = onpager_delivery_target.ops_alerts.id
}

resource "onpager_escalation_chain" "team_channels" {
  team_id = onpager_team_alert_channel.ops_alerts.team_id
  name    = "Notify team channels"
  steps   = [{ kind = "notify_channel", channel_sources = ["team"] }]
}

resource "onpager_escalation_rule" "warning" {
  team_id    = var.team_id
  name       = "Warning alerts"
  cel_source = "severity == \"warning\""
  chain_id   = onpager_escalation_chain.team_channels.id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `channel_id` (String) UUID of the delivery channel. It must be enabled when creating a target. Changing the channel replaces the target. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this target is enabled. Defaults to true. OnPager creates the target enabled. For false, the provider then disables it with a separate update. Disabled targets remain readable and can be re-enabled by UUID. Destroy disables the target and preserves its canonical destination.
- `snapshot_json` (String, Sensitive) Immutable provider-specific destination as a JSON object, typically supplied with `jsonencode`. Required on creation and replacement. Control validates the object for the selected channel and limits the whole encoded request to 8192 bytes. Terraform stores the sensitive configured string in state. Refresh preserves it because the API hides the destination. Omit it after import to manage enabled state. Supplying it after import or changing the destination requests replacement.

### Read-Only

- `contract_version` (String) Delivery provider contract version reported by the channel.
- `id` (String) Stable nonzero canonical lowercase OnPager UUID.
- `kind` (String) Delivery provider kind reported by the channel, such as bot or zvonok.

## Routing to a chat

The example creates the `ops-alerts` destination in an enabled Pachca bot's
addressing scope. The team alert catalog binds its UUID to the team. For alerts
already routed to that team, the warning rule selects a chain that notifies
the team's alert channels. Other enabled bindings in that catalog also
participate. If the team already has a warning rule and chain, use the target
and binding with the existing routing configuration.

The JSON object follows the selected channel's API contract. For a Pachca
conversation, use the OnPager bot UUID, its Pachca account ID and the chat
name. Control validates the address locally. Destination resolution and message
delivery happen when the channel is used.

## Import

Import by target UUID. OnPager returns the channel, kind, contract version and
enabled state. It omits the immutable destination. Omit `snapshot_json` in the
resource configuration when adopting an existing target. Supplying a snapshot
for an imported target with no saved snapshot plans replacement.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_delivery_target.ops_alerts
  id = "44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_delivery_target.ops_alerts 44444444-4444-4444-8444-444444444444
```

## Lifecycle

The channel and snapshot are immutable. Terraform retains the configured
snapshot in sensitive state across refresh. Changing only equivalent JSON
formatting updates the saved spelling without an API write or replacement.
Control requires an enabled channel and initially
creates the target enabled. With `enabled = false`, Terraform then disables
the created target. If that update fails, state retains the UUID of the
enabled target. Updating `enabled` preserves the UUID.

Destroy disables the target and retains its UUID and history. A disabled target
still reserves its canonical address on that channel. To reuse that address
after destroy, import the retained UUID and set `enabled = true`. Creating a
duplicate returns HTTP 409. Protect state and saved plans containing recipient
addresses.

## Permissions

Read and import require `delivery_targets.read`. Creation requires
`delivery_targets.create`. Updating requires `delivery_targets.update` and
setting `enabled = false` also requires `delivery_targets.disable`. Destroy
requires `delivery_targets.disable`. These are tenant grants for a PAT or
service account. The example's team binding, chain and rule require their own
team-scoped grants.
